# ethereum-optimism/op-analytics Daily Update (Jul 8, 2026)
## OVERVIEW 
Today, development focused on addressing a recurring flake in `reth-optimism-node` integration tests, specifically a SIGSEGV during teardown. A new pull request was opened to tolerate removed getters in `SystemConfig 4.0.0`.

## KEY TECHNICAL DEVELOPMENTS
No completed work to report for this period.

## NEWLY OPENED PULL REQUESTS
- **Chainsmeta Update**: A new pull request, [#1799](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-analytics/pull/1799), was opened to update `chainsmeta` to tolerate removed getters in `SystemConfig 4.0.0`.

## CLOSED ISSUES
No closed issues to report for this period.

## NEW ISSUES
No new issues to report for this period.

## ACTIVE ISSUES
- **Flaky `reth-optimism-node` Integration Test SIGSEGV** ([#20973](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-analytics/issues/20973)): Discussions continued regarding the non-deterministic SIGSEGV during the teardown of the `reth-optimism-node::it p2p_version::peers_negotiate_eth_69` integration test. The latest comment confirms another occurrence of the flake, which caused a merge-queue check to fail for an unrelated Go-only change. The issue is characterized by the test body passing, but the binary crashing with a SIGSEGV during teardown, specifically signal 11. This behavior is consistent with previous observations and is believed to be a race condition during runtime teardown, potentially related to an orphan OS thread accessing Tokio internals that are concurrently being freed. The issue is considered non-deterministic and not tied to the PRs it affects.
